Project File 04 / Founder Work

TapeItOut —
make hardware easier to try.

A semiconductor tooling effort spanning open-source ASIC flow orchestration and automated quality-of-results (QoR) benchmarking.

Yosys · LibreLane · OpenROAD · OpenSTA ● Building Flow Engine
01 / The immediate work
02 / Product direction
03 / The line between them

The immediate work

My current founder work is flow automation around open-source ASIC tools: synthesis, floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis (CTS), routing, and static timing analysis (STA), with regression automation and QoR reporting.

Current principle: Every run should leave a clear, auditable record—what passed, what failed, what is inconclusive, and which log artifacts support the claim.

The longer product direction

TapeItOut’s broader vision is an accessible, reproducible environment for chip design: start with clear constraints, simulate, revise, inspect DRC/LVS violations visually, and gradually move toward FPGA prototyping and ASIC tapeouts.

What I am not claiming

The full creative platform is not presented here as a finished SaaS product. Current work is focused on flow automation scripts and proving that the core workflow delivers repeatable QoR closure before expanding it.

What comes next

Keep the execution path reproducible across Linux environments, make timing and congestion heatmaps understandable, and validate the workflow with real student designers before scaling the tooling.
